The release design correctly moves immutable-release and public-channel preflight ahead of App-token minting and tag creation at [8b05a612-plan.md:325](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-8b05a612/dev/active/8b05a612-plan.md:325). One security-critical architectural component remains unspecified, described in Finding 1.

## Decomposition and dependencies

Pass on task ordering. Remediation precedes blocking audits; server shutdown precedes the image; the replacement image precedes topology removal; all source-changing work converges at the freeze; candidate validation precedes producers; assembly precedes staging and rehearsal; preflight precedes the final tag; publication follows it.

The external dependencies are real and appropriately placed at the freeze boundary. The core-maintenance handoff now explicitly requires closing `6eb585bc` before the production-readiness freeze at [6eb585bc-handoff.md:35](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-8b05a612/dev/active/6eb585bc-handoff.md:35), consistent with the plan’s freeze prerequisites at [8b05a612-plan.md:243](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-8b05a612/dev/active/8b05a612-plan.md:243).

## Risks and actionability

The risk register is otherwise extensive and provides concrete mitigations at [8b05a612-plan.md:364](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-8b05a612/dev/active/8b05a612-plan.md:364). However, the release evidence and transition ledger are security-critical state machines, and their persistence/coordination design is absent. That prevents the affected leaves from being executed without re-deriving a central part of the design.

## Prior review feedback

All three previous findings are addressed:

- The complete public-state preflight now occurs before token minting and final-tag creation at [8b05a612-plan.md:328](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-8b05a612/dev/active/8b05a612-plan.md:328).
- Docker now fixes and tests repository-root search behavior at [8b05a612-plan.md:195](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-8b05a612/dev/active/8b05a612-plan.md:195).
- The core-maintenance handoff now reflects D-14 at [6eb585bc-handoff.md:9](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-8b05a612/dev/active/6eb585bc-handoff.md:9).

## Findings

1. **F1 — High, blocking, issue-impact:** The cross-run evidence store and publication transition ledger have no specified persistence or trust contract. The freeze creates an evidence record “outside the source tree” ([8b05a612-plan.md:244](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-8b05a612/dev/active/8b05a612-plan.md:244)), a separately triggered candidate run must retrieve and authenticate it ([8b05a612-plan.md:253](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-8b05a612/dev/active/8b05a612-plan.md:253)), and publication requires durable prepared/completed records around every mutation ([8b05a612-plan.md:338](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-8b05a612/dev/active/8b05a612-plan.md:338)). Yet the orchestration leaf specifies only evidence schemas, not where records live, how later runs locate and authenticate them, retention and permissions, atomic publication, or crash recovery. This is especially load-bearing around the external, 2FA-protected `npm stage approve` step at line 339, which [npm documents as an interactive maintainer action](https://docs.npmjs.com/staged-publishing/). The repository has no existing release-ledger primitive to reuse. The plan must choose and specify the durable store and exact handoff protocol before fan-out; otherwise engineers must invent the security and resumability model during implementation. References: `@/issue/8b05a612/requirement/REQ-03`, `REQ-04`, `REQ-05`, `REQ-10`.
